$comment: Scoop manifest template. The release workflow substitutes 0.5.35,
https://yoink.cdn.jumpmind.cloud/yoink/0.5.35/yoink-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip and 1b25e6f1f37cb73dee54de5608a84b914c8503c39726e4a608fed8bf495a8aac and commits the result to the bucket repository.
https://yoink.cdn.jumpmind.cloud/yoink/0.5.35/yoink-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip is on the public downloads CDN, never a GitHub release: this
repository is private, so a GitHub URL is a 404 for everyone who would
install from a public bucket. There is no `checkver`/`autoupdate` for the
same reason: the release workflow pushes the new manifest itself, and
the GitHub API it would poll is not open to the public either.
1b25e6f1f37cb73dee54de5608a84b914c8503c39726e4a608fed8bf495a8aac is read from the .sha256 the release publishes beside the
archive, the same one the patched PowerShell installer verifies against,
so there is exactly one published hash per archive.
post_install: Write-Host 'yoink installed. Run `yoink doctor` to check it over.'
